born.why: The code prioritizes avoiding known poisons based on exact trait matches, uses "taste" to safely identify new fruits before committing to "carry", and only switches to immediate "eat" when starvation is imminent.

The code prioritizes starvation avoidance, then uses diary history to distinguish between known poisonous species (avoid) and safe ones (eat), while using trait-based caution for new species only when sufficient data exists, preventing premature avoidance of beneficial fruits due to limited experience.

The code prioritizes survival by checking for known poisons in the diary, uses innate instinct as a heuristic for unknown fruits to balance risk and reward, and implements a "taste" strategy for safe-to-learn situations to build knowledge without starving.

The code prioritizes survival by eating when starving, uses trait-sharing to avoid known poisons, and distinguishes between carrying proven tasty fruits home versus tasting unproven ones to expand the diary.

This code improves survival by distinguishing between clear benefits, neutral outcomes, and poison using trait matching, prioritizing data gathering via tasting when safe, and eating only when hungry or certain of safety to avoid starvation while minimizing risk.

The code uses past experience with a fruit species to determine safety, prioritizing eating only if the species is known safe or if starvation risk is imminent, otherwise tasting to verify or leaving to avoid poison.

The updated code prioritizes carrying safe fruits to the pantry for efficient resource management, avoids species with confirmed poison unless starving, and uses trait-based analogy for unknown fruits to gather safety data through tasting only when necessary.

This code prioritizes carrying the target fruit, uses a weighted history of similar traits (key, smell, shape) to classify safety, eats known-safe foods when hungry, tastes unknowns for learning unless starving, and avoids strong poison signals even at high hunger by tasting rather than eating whole, balancing survival against information gathering.
